quotes.text: # Accept a payment through local bank transfers in Nigeria
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: The transaction amount must be between 500 NGN and 100,000,000 NGN.
Listen for these events rather than waiting on a callback from the client.

findings: November's parent capture replaces detailed May Checkout and Direct API sections with links to the same two variants. It establishes topic and navigation only, with no substantive behavior evidence from either target (new raw lines 5–12, old raw lines 4–14 and 103–111, diff lines 4–12 and 294–297).

Source lines 17–28 accurately retain the May method identity and compatibility examples, but present the manual Checkout list as a general step and omit the historic dynamic route in old raw lines 8–14. Distinguish US business and NGN/500–100,000,000 Checkout prerequisites (old raw lines 20–44) from the Direct API wording at lines 107–132. Date hosted success_url and embedded embedded_page/return_url samples (old raw lines 46–97), and route current version questions to the separate API references.

Source line 32 promotes payment_method_data.type into a creation requirement. Old raw lines 128–132 enumerate amount, NGN and method types. Lines 134–146 additionally illustrate payment_method_data.type in a Node.js example. Label it as shown in the creation example, separate from the May Stripe.js browser confirmation sample at lines 220–264. The Nigeria concept line 73 repeats the overstatement.

Source lines 35–37 list redirect identifiers and test outcomes but omit verifying the PaymentIntent status before displaying the result and the browser-callback fulfillment caveat. Old raw lines 267–282 differentiate the returned Intent ID/client secret, the test API-key scenario from requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method, and completion events visible via Dashboard, webhook or partner solution. A browser return is insufficient for shipping or order confirmation. Date and qualify the reciprocal concept lines 74–82 and the Stripe index/company routes.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The dated 2026-05-08 detailed guide documents Nigerian customer local bank transfer through a Nigerian MoR service provider checkout, authentication/authorization and site return. May Checkout configuration includes dynamic or manual selection, US businesses and NGN-only line items, the 500–100,000,000 NGN amount range and payment-only mode (old raw lines 8–101).

May Direct API separates merchant server PaymentIntent creation and client-secret delivery from the Stripe.js Dahlia publishable-key confirmation and return_url on the browser (old raw lines 113–151 and 220–272). Preserve status verification, the requires_action test transitions under test keys and fulfillment using independently verified completion events rather than a redirect callback (old raw lines 267–294).
conflicts: Source lines 26 and 32 and the Nigeria concept lines 72–73 repeat the May sample's writable payment_method_types without API-version scope. Separate 2026-09-30.endive changelog captures remove the writable field on Checkout Session creation and PaymentIntent create/update/confirm, and point to dynamic selection or allowed/excluded filters (Checkout changelog raw lines 7–23 and Payment Intents/Setup Intents changelog raw lines 7–24). Endive filtering may omit an incompatible method, and the read-only computed response property is distinct. Keep both dated, add a reciprocal warning to the acceptance source and concept, and avoid using the unread November variant URLs to prescribe a specific new Naira integration.

May Checkout detailed guide excludes setup/subscription modes (old raw lines 28–32). The separate May Nigeria family overview labeled bank-transfer recurring Coming soon, while its November matrix lists one-time Yes and recurring No and adds a preview invite-request step (raw/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods-2025.md lines 96–104 and November country overview lines 70–103 and 105–117). A dated roadmap cell, request for access, Dashboard setting or partner redirect is not approval or proof of live transfer recurring support. Keep reciprocal overview and concept routing. Distinguish Naira cards from ng_bank_transfer and the local partner-MoR route from the separate Stripe-as-MoR Managed Payments product.
unresolved_questions: This November parent does not establish the versions, current behavior or account eligibility of its linked variants. The separate general Endive changelogs establish their endpoint rules, not validation of either Nigerian bank-transfer path.

source_assessments.reason: Date the May recipes, restore the historical dynamic path and payment-status boundary, correct the creation sample overstatement, and use reciprocal version and access warnings. The November parent is a navigation reference.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-bank-transfer/accept-a-payment, the November capture gives the topic and links to Checkout and Direct API. The parent has no details on setup, eligibility or payment states (new raw lines 5-12). The May guide describes a Nigerian customer transferred to the local merchant-of-record provider to authenticate and authorize, then sent back to the merchant's site. The Checkout variant offers dynamic selection or a historical manual list, and its compatibility rules specify US businesses, NGN-only line items, 500–100,000,000 NGN and payment mode without setup or subscriptions (old raw lines 8-44). Its hosted and embedded examples use distinct navigation settings. In Direct API, the server creates a PaymentIntent with amount, ngn and ng_bank_transfer listed in the May instructions. The example also includes payment_method_data.type. The browser uses the client secret and publishable-key Stripe.js to confirm with that type and return_url (old raw lines 113-151 and 220-264). The return parameters identify the Intent and its client secret so the page can verify status. Test-key examples transition from requires_action to succeeded or requires_payment_method. Independently verify completion for fulfillment, with payment_intent.succeeded visible through Dashboard, webhook or partner solution (old raw lines 267-294). source-stripe-ng-bank-transfer-accept-payment.md retains the historical core but overstates the creation example field and leaves out dynamic Checkout and the status-verification boundary.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-bank-transfer/accept-a-payment, the November change is navigation: the same two historical variants appear as links, and their November bodies remain unverified (new raw lines 5-12). Keep the US/NGN and Checkout mode/amount prerequisites, distinct hosted success_url and embedded return_url examples, and client/server Direct API and test-mode states dated to May (old raw lines 8-101, 113-151 and 220-282). In source-stripe-ng-bank-transfer-accept-payment.md and its reciprocal Nigeria concept, qualify payment_method_data.type at server creation as a sample field and preserve verified completion as distinct from browser return. The separate 2026-09-30.endive changelogs remove writable payment_method_types on Checkout Session creation and applicable PaymentIntent requests and describe dynamic selection or allowed/excluded compatibility filtering. Warn reciprocally and keep those changes separate from the November parent capture. The country overview's November invite-request step and Yes/No one-time/recurring matrix qualify use independently of the historical May Coming soon wording. An invite request is distinct from approval and the transfer path is distinct from Naira cards and Stripe Managed Payments.
